freeze_rule: Frozen before any protocol-v2-scoped forecast has been graded by outlier_grade_forecasts. Changing any value requires a new protocol version (v3) with an independent rationale of its own; v1 and v2 are both preserved unmodified, exactly as v1's own freeze_rule already required of whatever superseded it.

source_documents.role: CB-15 spec, phase P5 and gate G8
shared DB contract names this file codes to (editorial_forecasts, outlier_recipe_models, idea_scores, outlier_forecast_grades, own_post_boost_marks, cron job names)
industry-recipe pre-registration (estimator, validation pass rule, paid handling, minimum_data) this file's industry_prior class and grading section read from
live state grounding: editorial_forecasts row counts, own-account floors, protocol v1 contradiction (db/229), no engagement endpoint, no boost field
db/229 build notes (trigger design, the lock-wait fix, the readback bug)

supersedes.relationship: v2 extends v1's contract; it does not replace or invalidate it. v1 stays byte-identical on disk (verified by file_sha256 above at the time this file was authored). Every verdict already rendered under v1 stands. See canonical.deviation_records for the one clause v2 explicitly supersedes (the forecast store).

meta_rule: This protocol changes how later CB runs are judged: it ratifies the live forecast store, adds a second scored model class, opens a second endpoint, and sets the grading schedule and floor every future run's G8-equivalent gate will check against. Per the CB-15 spec (P5), a protocol change of this kind requires an independent H1 review before the orchestrator adopts it. That review belongs in O/review/H1-PROTOCOL-V2.md, written by an agent other than lane P, and the orchestrator's transcription of it is what actually ratifies this file for G8 purposes -- this file alone is a proposal, not a self-ratifying freeze. (The first H1 pass on this file FAILED on two findings -- future-dated declared_at, and an unpinned idea/draft stage for industry_validated/industry_model_version -- both fixed in this revision; see canonical.forecast_row_columns and feature_extension.declared_at_provenance.)

canonical.relationship_to_v1: v2 extends v1; it does not replace it. v1's own_reach endpoint, its candidate model, its display_conditions and its exclusion_reason_codes all remain in force unchanged and are inherited by reference. v2 adds: a ratified forecast store, a second (industry_prior) model class, a declared feature-key extension, an optional secondary endpoint, a grading schedule, paid/boosted handling, and an explicit minimum-data floor for grading. v1 stays byte-identical on disk; any forecast row written before this file's frozen_at is read under v1 only.

deviation_records.what_actually_happened: db/229 (CB-14, applied and H2-reviewed 2026-09-24) created a new physical, append-only table `editorial_forecasts` plus `editorial_publication_links` and `editorial_forecast_failures`, written by 3 AFTER triggers on carousel_drafts (lock_timeout 250ms, never raises inside a publisher transaction; CB-14 fixed a version that could stall a publisher write under a held lock). Live state at CB-15 P0 (2026-09-24, AU/D): 15 rows (ivan 3, risedtc 10, arch 2), all status=insufficient_data, recorded by a 14:02:21Z backfill; editorial_forecast_failures = 0.
deviation_records.ratification: editorial_forecasts (db/229) is hereby ratified as THE forecast store for every forecast graded under protocol v2 or later. This is a deviation from v1's design, recorded in writing rather than silently overridden, exactly as v1's own freeze_rule requires ('changing any value requires a new protocol version with an independent rationale; the prior version is preserved').
deviation_records.rationale: v1's 'no_new_physical_table' clause was accurate when v1 was frozen (2026-09-21): no requirement at that time needed a new table. CB-14 subsequently built and populated editorial_forecasts for reasons outside this protocol's original scope (an insert-time forecast plus outcome/failure capture triggered directly off carousel_drafts, not off a brief-version edit cycle). Reusing editorial_brief_versions.payload.forecast now would mean maintaining two disagreeing forecast stores with no reconciliation path; ratifying the table that already exists, is already written by a reviewed trigger, and already carries the live rows is the only choice that does not fork the data.

forecast_persistence.store: editorial_forecasts (db/229), one row per forecast event
forecast_persistence.write_path: 3 AFTER triggers on carousel_drafts: insert-time forecast write, mark-published outcome capture, and failure logging. CB-15 lane M/B extend this trigger additively to also fill the industry_* columns declared below; the trigger never UPDATEs a row it did not just insert.
forecast_persistence.append_only: Existing editorial_forecasts rows are never updated or deleted (PLAN.md: 'existing rows stay append-only'; G8 MUSTNOT: 'an existing forecast row updated'). A later observation, a later industry score, or a later grade is always a new row in a different table (outlier_forecast_grades), never a rewrite of the forecast row itself.
forecast_persistence.v1_store_status: editorial_brief_versions.payload.forecast + editorial_brief_artifacts (v1's store) is not deleted or disabled by this ratification. It is simply not the store any v2-scoped forecast uses. If any pre-db/229 forecast was ever written there, it remains readable under v1's own contract and is not migrated.

own_reach.decision_role: primary, own-post logistic-regression class exactly as v1 defined it (regularized logistic regression, l2, lambda=1.0, features: format/client one-hot, log1p body length, hour/dow sin-cos, log1p baseline median, baseline n). Nothing about this class changes in v2.

industry_prior.decision_role: A second, independent prior carried on the same forecast row, produced by the CB-15 industry-outlier recipe (PREREG.json estimator: within-author Mantel-Haenszel log-odds, conditional-logit family) rather than by v1's own-post logistic model. own_reach and industry_prior are never combined into one score; each is stored, reported and graded separately.
industry_prior.stage_gating: PREREG.json stage_gating: the idea-stage model orders ideas; the draft-stage model 'is validated the same way and its verdict travels with forecasts only'. v2 therefore treats the two stages asymmetrically on the forecast row -- see canonical.forecast_row_columns below for exactly which physical column or jsonb key each stage's score, model_version and validated flag lives in. This is an H1 review fix (finding 2): v1-draft of this file left industry_validated/industry_model_version single-valued, which let a later writer pick whichever stage's flag was favourable. They are now pinned to the draft stage only.

components.idea_score: idea_scores.score for the matching row (client_id, idea_table, idea_ref, stage='idea', model_version) -- written to the flat column editorial_forecasts.industry_idea_score
components.idea_model_version: outlier_recipe_models.model_version for the idea-stage fit -- written to editorial_forecasts.industry_contributions.idea_model_version (jsonb key, NOT a flat column; see forecast_row_columns)
components.idea_validated: outlier_recipe_models.validated for the idea-stage fit -- written to editorial_forecasts.industry_contributions.idea_validated (jsonb key, NOT a flat column)
components.draft_score: idea_scores.score for the matching row at stage='draft' -- written to the flat column editorial_forecasts.industry_draft_score
components.model_version: outlier_recipe_models.model_version (primary key) for the DRAFT-stage fit that produced draft_score -- written to the flat column editorial_forecasts.industry_model_version. This key name (bare 'model_version', no stage prefix) is reserved for the draft stage because PREREG.json says the draft verdict is the one that 'travels with forecasts'; the idea-stage equivalent is always named idea_model_version and never written here.
components.validated: outlier_recipe_models.validated boolean for the DRAFT-stage fit, computed per PREREG.json validation.pass_rule: validated iff auc_ci_low > 0.55 AND top_decile_hit_rate >= 1.5 * base_rate AND loao_auc > 0.55, AND validation.minimum_data is met (>= 20 test outliers AND >= 5 test authors holding an outlier); otherwise 'unvalidated (insufficient data)' or 'unvalidated'. Written to the flat column editorial_forecasts.industry_validated. Same stage-pinning rule as model_version above: the idea-stage equivalent is always named idea_validated.

industry_prior.decision_rule: An unvalidated industry_prior (validated=false in any form, including insufficient-data), at EITHER stage, IS recorded on every forecast row -- industry_idea_score, industry_draft_score, industry_model_version, industry_validated (draft stage) and industry_contributions.idea_model_version / .idea_validated (idea stage) all get written -- but MUST NOT be used to decide anything: not idea ordering, not format choice, not a ballot ranking, not a grading weight, not a display sort. This mirrors CB-15 spec fork 4 verbatim ('a client whose recipe fails the pre-registered holdout gets scores labelled unvalidated, shown greyed and never used for ordering... the score rows are still recorded, so the grader can judge them later').
industry_prior.grading_use: The scheduled grader (below) MAY compare an unvalidated industry_prior's score to the real outcome after the fact -- that comparison is exactly how a currently-unvalidated recipe earns validation later. Using it to decide anything BEFORE that grading has run is what this rule forbids.

forecast_row_columns.source: O/PLAN.md shared DB contract: editorial_forecasts gains 5 industry columns, filled by the db/229 trigger

industry_model_version.note: Bare, unprefixed name is reserved for the draft-stage model_version because PREREG.json stage_gating says the draft verdict 'travels with forecasts'. Never holds the idea-stage model_version.

shape.contributions: [{indicator, beta, words}, ...] draft-stage, per idea_scores.contributions shape
shape.idea_model_version: outlier_recipe_models.model_version for the idea-stage fit (H1 finding 2: named key, required)
shape.idea_validated: outlier_recipe_models.validated for the idea-stage fit (H1 finding 2: named key, required)

industry_contributions.note: This is the ONLY place the idea-stage model_version/validated are recorded on the forecast row. A reader wanting the idea-stage verdict must read industry_contributions.idea_model_version / .idea_validated, never industry_model_version / industry_validated, which are draft-stage only.

feature_extension.extends: dataset.py ALLOWED_FEATURE_KEYS, the closed set of 8: format, client, topic_category, body_chars, published_hour, published_dow, baseline_median, baseline_n
feature_extension.declared_at_provenance: H1 review fix (finding 1): the first draft of this file used a fixed future timestamp (2026-09-24T21:00:00Z), which is unverifiable by construction and would have falsely excluded any forecast the cb15b trigger writes before that clock time -- exactly the rows G8 and the P6 live trace need to count. declared_at is now the real wall-clock instant this file was generated, captured programmatically (datetime.now(UTC)) and cross-stamped against the live Supabase server clock in the sibling file protocol-v2.commit.json, the same way PREREG.commit.json stamps PREREG.json.
feature_extension.invariant: declared_at <= min(recorded_at) over every editorial_forecasts row where industry_model_version IS NOT NULL. In words: no row that actually carries an industry score may have been recorded before this extension was declared. cb15b (the migration that adds and starts filling these columns) is not applied as of this file's declared_at, so the invariant holds trivially now (the set of qualifying rows is empty) and becomes a live check once cb15b ships: G8's check must confirm it holds over the full table, not just re-assert it by construction.
feature_extension.declared_before_use: As of this file's declared_at, no code path in dataset.py, evaluate.py or forecast.py reads or writes these four keys (confirmed by inspection at authoring time) and no CB-15 decision (idea ordering, format choice, ballot ranking) consumes them yet. The declaration therefore precedes any decision that could use it, satisfying the ordering the CB-15 spec requires for a feature extension, and precedes cb15b itself (not yet applied at declared_at), satisfying the invariant above.

key_definitions.industry_idea_score: numeric or null; industry_prior.components.idea_score at forecast time; null when no idea_scores row exists yet for the idea
key_definitions.industry_draft_score: numeric or null; industry_prior.components.draft_score at forecast time; null before a draft exists
key_definitions.industry_validated: boolean, DRAFT STAGE ONLY (H1 finding 2 fix); industry_prior.components.validated, copied at write time. The idea-stage validated flag is a different value, stored under the named key industry_contributions.idea_validated -- see canonical.forecast_row_columns. The underlying draft-stage flag may later flip for a NEW outlier_recipe_models.model_version; that never rewrites this forecast row's copy (append-only), so a forecast's industry_validated always reflects what was true at the moment it was forecast, not what is true now.
key_definitions.industry_model_version: text or null, DRAFT STAGE ONLY (H1 finding 2 fix); industry_prior.components.model_version at forecast time; the join key back to outlier_recipe_models for the grader. The idea-stage model_version is a different value, stored under the named key industry_contributions.idea_model_version -- see canonical.forecast_row_columns. Before this fix a later writer could have populated either stage's value here interchangeably; that ambiguity is now closed.

feature_extension.closed_set_note: industry_contributions (jsonb, holding idea_model_version and idea_validated among other keys) is a real editorial_forecasts column per O/PLAN.md, but it is NOT one of dataset.py's ALLOWED_FEATURE_KEYS: it is a structured audit/detail payload, not a flat model-input feature. dataset-v2.patch therefore adds exactly these 4 flat keys and no more.
feature_extension.application_rule: This extension applies ONLY to forecasts recorded at or after declared_at, per the invariant above. A forecast row written before declared_at -- including the 15 live editorial_forecasts rows from the 2026-09-24T14:02:21Z backfill (ivan 3, risedtc 10, arch 2, all status=insufficient_data) -- has no industry_* columns populated. The evaluator/grader reads that as industry_model_version=null, meaning 'no industry prior was declared yet for this forecast', never as a zero or missing score to be imputed.
feature_extension.code_path: dataset.py is owned by ivan-inbox, outside lane P's OWNS (O/build/protocol/**). A proposed, UNAPPLIED patch adding the four keys to ALLOWED_FEATURE_KEYS is staged at O/build/protocol/dataset-v2.patch for whichever lane or future run applies it under its own write scope.

primary.status: primary, inherited unchanged from protocol v1
primary.note: Every v1 field governing this endpoint (label window, baseline, partitions, dependence_block, baselines_predeclared, candidate_model=own_reach, display_conditions, statuses, exclusion_reason_codes) stays exactly as v1 defines it. v2 does not re-freeze it; it is repeated here only as a pointer, not a copy of record.

secondary.status: secondary; declared for the first time in this file
secondary.endpoint_definition: For one own published post, (reactions + 3 * reposts) observed at a capture 7-14 days after publication, greater than that author's own trailing median of the same computed metric over the author's prior published, non-boosted, retained observations.
secondary.relationship_to_industry_metric: Uses the same 3x repost weight as the industry outlier score (PREREG.json corpus.metric = likes + 3*reposts) for consistency, but the own-side metric is 'reactions' (LinkedIn's own-analytics field, which is broader than 'likes') because that is the field own-metric collectors retain. This naming difference is intentional and disclosed, not a typo.
secondary.observation_window: 7-14 days post-publication, matching PLAN.md's outlier_corpus_v observation preference (prefer 7-14d, else earliest reading older than 14d as age_class=late, else latest reading under 7d as age_class=early_only, recorded on every row).
secondary.constraints: Declared, not yet fit: no candidate_model exists for this endpoint in v2. It inherits v1's baseline/label discipline (unknown is never zero, a label exists only with a real retained observation in-window, own boosted posts excluded per own_post_boost_marks) and v1's display_status vocabulary (insufficient_data / experimental / validated_for_scope), but starts at insufficient_data or experimental for every client until a future protocol version (v3+) registers a fit and a pass rule for it, exactly as v1 required for the primary endpoint. It NEVER substitutes for the primary endpoint and is never shown as validated by inheriting the primary endpoint's status.
secondary.rationale_for_declaring_now: Ivan's own words (spec Authority): 'we were looking for overall outliers not just to prioritize a format'. Impressions-only measurement misses posts that get shared more than seen (reposts) or reacted to strongly (reactions) relative to impressions; declaring the endpoint now, before any decision uses it, keeps the option open for CB-16 without letting a later run declare-and-use it in the same breath, which this protocol's own rule forbids.

grading.schedule: weekly, pg_cron job cb15_forecast_grader (Tue 07:30 UTC per O/PLAN.md), running inside Supabase -- outside ~/Desktop, which matters because launchd cannot read ~/Desktop (memory launchd-cannot-read-desktop-tcc-2026-09-02) and pg_cron is not subject to that restriction.
grading.maturity_rule: a forecast is graded only once its target post's outcome has matured: >= 7 days after publication (matching v1's target_age_days=7 / tolerance_hours=24 window for the primary endpoint; the secondary engagement endpoint above uses its own 7-14 day window). A forecast whose post has not yet matured is left ungraded this cycle, not graded on a partial/early read.
grading.store: outlier_forecast_grades, append-only (O/PLAN.md). A re-grade with better/later data is always a NEW row, never an edit of a prior grade.
grading.grader_function: outlier_grade_forecasts(p_run_key text) per O/PLAN.md; the weekly cron supplies a fresh p_run_key per fire so repeat runs are idempotent and each run is individually inspectable.
grading.notification: posts one inbox feed line per client with a REGISTERED src (O/PLAN.md; memory shared-page-open-tracker-2026-09-21: an unregistered src rings silently -- this registration is load-bearing, not decorative).
grading.dry_run_requirement: G8 requires one dry grading pass saved as evidence before this protocol counts as proven live, in addition to the schedule existing.

paid_and_boosted_handling.own_posts: own_post_boost_marks (append-only: client_id, post_ref, boosted boolean, marked_by, marked_at; latest mark per post_ref wins) excludes a boosted own post from (a) the own trailing-median baseline denominator used by both the primary and secondary endpoints, and (b) own-side grading counts. A post carrying no mark is treated as unboosted -- Ivan marks manually because he knows when he boosts (spec Authority), so silence is a real organic default here, unlike the industry side below.
paid_and_boosted_handling.industry_posts: paid_status on audn_competitor_posts / competitor_posts / competitor_post_snapshots (organic|paid|unknown). 'paid' rows are excluded from the industry_prior recipe's baselines and findings, and from any grading that reads them. 'unknown' rows are kept and counted in every reported number (spec Authority: 'unknown is counted... never silently treated as organic'; PREREG.json corpus.paid), including grading denominators, with the unknown count disclosed beside the grade exactly as PREREG.json discloses it beside the outlier count.
paid_and_boosted_handling.asymmetry_is_intentional: own posts default to organic-unless-marked; industry posts default to unknown-unless-mapped. This is deliberate -- Ivan controls his own boost knowledge directly, while industry paid/sponsored detection depends on whether the scraping actor exposes a sponsored field (W-S1/W-S2 map it when available) -- and is stated here so a future protocol version does not 'fix' it into a false symmetry.

minimum_data.requirement: 20 clean posts per client before any grade counts for that client, same as v1
minimum_data.v1_anchor: protocol v1 canonical.baseline.min_prior_observations = 20 -- the same number governs both v1's baseline-eligibility floor and this grading floor, by explicit choice rather than coincidence.
minimum_data.distinct_from_prereg_floor: PREREG.json validation.minimum_data (< 20 test outliers OR < 5 test authors holding an outlier = unvalidated) gates the RECIPE's validated flag on the industry corpus. This clause is a separate, own-account floor: a client's own account needs >= 20 clean posts before outlier_grade_forecasts will produce any grade for that client at all, independent of whether the recipe itself is validated.
minimum_data.clean_definition: 'clean' = not excluded by any protocol exclusion_reason_code (inherited from v1) AND not boosted (own_post_boost_marks.boosted=true) AND not paid_status='paid'.
minimum_data.current_state_2026_09_24: Ivan 8, RISE 12, ARCH 6 -- all below the 20-post floor (AU/D). Projected dates to reach 20 clean posts: RISE ~2026-10-12, Ivan ~2026-10-25, ARCH ~2026-11-08 (AU/D; assumes ~100% future-capture qualification rate, which AU/D marks CANNOT JUDGE -- these are projections, not commitments).
